title: Warn at load when a 0.1 task-coupled type inherits a closed base status enum lacking the rollup values (DEC-192 (8))
description:
DEC-192 (8), option A (opum-ai/opum-doc#1023), ruled 2026-10-14 on a finding raised during the LCLI-728 review at opum-ai/lore-cli#591.

THE FINDING, as measured. A 0.1 task-coupled type that INHERITS a closed base `status` enum gets its own rollup vocabulary refused by the generated TYPE SCHEMA, not by the lifecycle check. Concretely, on a 0.1 profile declaring `[base.fields] status = { enum = ["draft", "approved"] }`, a `type: "Story"` document with `status: "done"` is refused with `invalid Story frontmatter: status: Invalid option: expected one of "draft"|"approved"`. The schema runs on every OKF version, so it fires before `validateLifecycleStatus` is consulted, and the 0.1 carve-out never gets the chance to apply. A profile that closes `status` on a task-coupled 0.1 type has closed its own rollup key.

That is in tension with DEC-192 (1), whose proof included "a 0.1 Story with `status: done` still passing" — which is true of the BUILT-IN profile, where `status` is an OPEN optional string, but not of a profile that closes it.

WHAT DEC-192 (8) RULES — a WARNING, never an error, because public profiles that load today must keep loading:
- ADD a named load-time warning. It must not become an error and must not change what loads.
- TRIGGER: a 0.1 task-coupled type INHERITS a closed base `status` enum that lacks `todo`, `in-progress` and `done`.
- The warning NAMES the type, the inherited enum, and the remedy: declare `status` on that type — either open, or including the rollup values.
- PROVE IT BOTH WAYS: such a profile warns, naming all three; the built-in profile stays SILENT, and so does a profile where the remedy has been applied.
- DEC-192 (1)'s "a 0.1 Story with `done` still passes" is hereby SCOPED to the built-in profile and to profiles where the type's `status` is open or includes the rollup values. That scoping is part of this task's deliverable — the record that carries (1) should say it, and the test that proves (1) should say which fixture it holds for.

SCOPE NOTE. This is a WARNING-and-scoping task. It adds a finding and adjusts a claim's scope; it does NOT change any load, validate or check outcome, and it must not turn the refusal above into an acceptance — the schema refusing a closed enum on 0.1 stays exactly as it is. A reader who wants the rollup key to work on such a type applies the remedy the warning names.

RELATED, not in this task: the review that raised it (LCLI-728) deliberately did NOT change behaviour for it, per the leader's ruling.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A profile whose OKF 0.1 task-coupled type INHERITS a closed base `status` enum lacking todo/in-progress/done produces a WARNING that names the type, the inherited enum, and the remedy (declare `status` on that type, open or including the rollup values).

The warning is never an error by default: it does not change any load, validate or check outcome, and the schema refusal of a document whose `status` is outside the closed enum stays exactly as it is.

Proved both ways: the offending profile warns naming all three; the built-in profile stays silent; and a profile where the remedy has been applied stays silent, on BOTH remedy arms. A mutation control reddens exactly the warning test that pins the DECLARED-versus-fallback distinction.
Exit codes, DEC-192 (10): without --strict the offending profile warns and `lore check` exits 0; with --strict the same profile FAILS; with --strict a built-in-profile repository passes.

DEC-192 (1) is scoped where this repository states it: the test proving that a 0.1 Story carrying `status: done` still passes says which fixture it holds for (the built-in profile, whose base `status` is open).

plan: Settle the surface: the ruling asks for a named load-time warning but names no command. Read as a warn-tier named check/validate finding emitted once per profile load, attributed to the profile file.
Detect the trigger from the compiled Profile: OKF 0.1, a type declaring the `tasks` field (profileTypeDeclaresField), whose MERGED status spec declares an enum that lacks the three rollup values.
Emit it once, not per document, and never as an error.
Prove both ways plus a mutation control, and scope the DEC-192 (1) test in this repository.
Gates: bun test, typecheck, lint, bun run lore check. CHANGELOG entry.
implementationNotes:
CLAIMED AND PLANNED (2026-10-14). Four acceptance criteria derived from the DEC-192 (8) ruling, which specified the trigger, what the warning must name, and a both-ways proof, but NOT the surface it appears on.

THE ONE READING I HAD TO MAKE, flagged for review rather than buried. The ruling says add a named load-time warning and names no command. Measured: loadProfile and compileProfile (src/core/profile.ts:395, :930) have no warning channel at all - LoadProfileOptions carries only root - and no profile-level warning exists anywhere today, only a comment at profile.ts:490 calling one a future nicety. So the warning cannot be produced inside the load call and must be emitted by the loaders callers. Read as a warn-tier NAMED finding in the existing Finding shape (Finding.rule is what named means here, beside the portability lint, this repository own precedent for a non-gating named warning), emitted ONCE per profile rather than per document, attributed to the profile file. Under that shape it is promoted only by an explicit --strict run, which is the documented behaviour of every warning in this tier and is not a change to what loads. Alternative if opum-doc prefers: a stderr advisory collector, which --strict never promotes. Flagged to the leader.

WHY THE BUILT-IN PROFILE IS SILENT, measured rather than assumed. [base.fields].status in storyConventionProfile is optionalString (profile.ts:1170, :1206) - kind string, NO enum - and no built-in type declares its own status. The built-in triple draft/stable/deprecated is a compiler FALLBACK (effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum, profile.ts:152), not a declared enum, so a rule keyed on a DECLARED closed base enum never fires. That mechanism is what the both-ways proof rests on.

TASK-COUPLED DETECTION, read from the code rather than invented: profileTypeDeclaresField(type, "tasks", profile) (profile.ts:1348) is how check decides a type supports task coupling (check.ts:593), and taskRollupFieldFor(version) (okf-version.ts:45) is the version-selected rollup key - status on 0.1, lore_task_status on 0.2. There is no isTaskCoupledType helper anywhere.

THE OPUM-DOC HALF, NOT MINE TO DO. The ruling says DEC-192 (1) claim should be scoped in the record that carries it, and that record lives in the opum-doc tracker, not this repository. The in-repo half (the test saying which fixture it holds for) is AC4. The tracker half is relayed to the leader.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION BY THE WORKING SESSION (2026-10-14), after the implementer froze f702d7c7. Gates re-run by me, not inherited: bun test 5138 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail across 151 files; typecheck exit 0; lint exit 0 with 14 pre-existing warnings and 1 info, none introduced; bun run lore check exit 0, 90 files, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing portability warnings, 4 agent profiles read, 0 over capacity.

A FALSE NEGATIVE FOUND IN THE BUILT HEAD, FIXED, AND PINNED. The implementer disclosed that the detector could not distinguish a DECLARED enum from the compiler fallback, guarded on the effective enum equalling the built-in triple, and documented a declared enum byte-equal to that triple as an unexercised false negative. Reproduced at f702d7c7 BEFORE touching anything: a 0.1 profile declaring [base.fields] status = { enum = ["draft","stable","deprecated"] } with a task-coupled Story reads SILENT, so AC1 was not met on that input. That IS a declared closed base enum lacking every rollup value, so the rule must fire. Fixed at 0bb54e1c by adding CompiledType.lifecycleStatusDeclared (merged.status.enum !== undefined) and guarding on DECLARED rather than on the value, which is also the condition the brief specified. Six-case matrix re-run: the declared-built-in-triple case now warns, the ruling example still warns, and both remedy arms, the 0.2 case, the non-coupled case and the built-in control all stay silent.

THE FIX IS PINNED BY THE ONLY TEST THAT CAN PIN IT. Mutation control run and PREDICTED FIRST: reverting the guard to the triple comparison leaves the rest of the file green and reddens exactly the new test (7 pass, 1 fail); reverted, 8 pass. Without that test the fix would have been unpinned, because every other assertion in the file passes under the old guard too.

THE DEC-192 (10) EXIT-CODE PROOFS, VERIFIED ON THE REAL CLI against fixture repositories rather than only in-process: the offending profile without --strict warns and exits 0; the same profile with --strict exits 6; a built-in-profile repository with --strict reads 0 warnings and exits 0.

AC2 VERIFIED ON THE REAL CLI TOO: with the warning in place, a Story carrying status: done on the closed-enum profile is still refused by the generated type schema - invalid Story frontmatter: status: Invalid option: expected one of draft|approved - exit 6. The warning names the collision; it does not resolve it.

DESIGN CHOICES, RECORDED. lore validate is deliberately NOT wired: validate is per-file and this finding is profile-scoped with no file, so wiring it would distort that model, and leaving it unwired keeps AC2 literally true. No docs change: no document states an exhaustive check-rule roster, so a new warn-tier rule leaves every one of them accurate, and no agent-profile capacity figure moves. RECONCILED_STATUSES is now exported from reconcile.ts so the three rollup values have one source rather than being respelled.

REQUEST CHANGES ON #604 AND THE FIX (2026-10-14, review round 2). The Stage 1 unit found one blocking defect and the leader confirmed it in the code: the version gate read the WRONG OBJECT. taskStatusEnumInheritedFindings returned early on profile.okfVersion, the producer profile own okf_version, while the schema that refuses a rollup status is built PER BUNDLE by profileForBundle, and DEC-192 (8) is scoped to a 0.1 BUNDLE task-coupled type. The unit also confirmed the round-1 declared-versus-fallback guard is correct, including the inheritance and open-declaration cases.

BOTH DIRECTIONS REPRODUCED AT bd1062a1 ON THE REAL CLI BEFORE ANY CHANGE, as asked. (a) FALSE NEGATIVE: a profile with okf_version = "0.2" and a closed base status enum over a bundle whose root index omits okf_version (legacy-missing, resolves to 0.1) - status: done was REFUSED by the type schema while the run reported 0 warnings, so the collision was real and unannounced. (b) FALSE POSITIVE: a okf_version = "0.1" profile over a bundle declaring 0.2 warned, though there the rollup key is lore_task_status and status is only the lifecycle key.

THE FIX. The detector now takes the scanned bundle STATES, evaluates each through profileForBundle, and gates on the resulting BUNDLE version, deduped by type so N 0.1 bundles still yield exactly ONE finding per offending type (DEC-192 (10) required once-per-profile, and two 0.1 bundles must not duplicate it). Re-run on the same fixtures after the fix: (a) warns alongside the schema error, (b) is silent, and the original 0.1-over-legacy-0.1 case still warns.

TESTS NOW VARY BUNDLE STATE, NOT ONLY profile.okf_version: a 0.2 bundle is silent for either producer version; a 0.2 producer profile over a 0.1 bundle warns; mixed and repeated bundle lists warn exactly once; every round-1 case stays green. Three end-to-end cases were added because the old built-in test was VACUOUS - with no .lore/profile.toml the detector is never reached, so it proved nothing.

MUTATION CONTROL: reverting the gate to the producer version reddens exactly the five tests that exercise bundle state and leaves the other nine green, the new (a) case among them; reverted, 14 pass.

GATES ON THE FIXED HEAD: bun test 5144 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail across 151 files; typecheck exit 0; lint exit 0 with 14 pre-existing warnings and 1 info (a FORMATTING error I introduced in the new test file was caught by lint and fixed before this run, which is why that count moved and came back); bun run lore check exit 0, 90 files, 0 errors, 4 agent profiles read, 0 over capacity.

DOC CORRECTIONS: the detector doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry both described the gate ambiguously and now both say the gate is the BUNDLE version.
finalSummary:
LCLI-730 adds a warn-tier lore check rule, task-status-enum-inherited (opum-ai/lore-cli#604). An OKF 0.1 task-coupled type whose DECLARED status enum is closed and omits every task-rollup value has closed its own rollup key - on 0.1 status IS that key - so a written status: done is refused by the generated type schema before any lifecycle check is reached. The warning names the type, the inherited enum and the remedy, is emitted once per profile load rather than per document, and is attributed to the profile file the load read. It changes no load, validate or check outcome.

Why this shape: DEC-192 (8) asked for a named load-time warning and named no command; loadProfile and compileProfile have no warning channel at all, so the warning is emitted by the loaders callers as a named finding beside the portability lint, this repository own precedent for a non-gating named warning. DEC-192 (10) ratified that surface and added the exit-code proofs. lore validate is deliberately not wired, since validate is per-file and this finding is profile-scoped with no file.

A FALSE NEGATIVE WAS FOUND IN REVIEW AND FIXED, which is the substance of this delivery rather than a footnote. The first implementation guarded on the effective enum equalling the built-in triple, so a profile declaring status = { enum = [draft, stable, deprecated] } on a 0.1 task-coupled type - a declared closed base enum lacking every rollup value, exactly the trigger - read SILENT. Reproduced at f702d7c7 before anything was changed, fixed at 0bb54e1c by adding CompiledType.lifecycleStatusDeclared and guarding on DECLARED rather than on the value, and pinned by a new test that is the ONLY one that reddens when the guard is reverted (7 pass, 1 fail; reverted, 8 pass).

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. Gates re-run by the working session on the frozen head, not inherited from the implementer: bun test 5138 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail across 151 files; typecheck exit 0; lint exit 0 with 14 pre-existing warnings, none introduced; bun run lore check exit 0 with 90 files, 0 errors and 4 agent profiles read, 0 over capacity. The DEC-192 (10) exit codes were proved on the real CLI against fixture repositories: the offending profile without --strict warns and exits 0; the same profile with --strict exits 6; a built-in-profile repository with --strict exits 0. AC2 was proved end-to-end the same way: with the warning in place a Story carrying status: done on the closed-enum profile is STILL refused by the type schema (exit 6), so the warning names the collision and does not resolve it. Both remedy arms, the 0.2 case and the non-coupled case are silent.

The PR carries the code; the completion rides the same branch, so the reviewed head carries the closed record.

REVIEW ROUND 2 (2026-10-14): the Stage 1 unit REQUESTED CHANGES on #604 for one blocking defect and the leader confirmed it. The version gate read the producer profile own okf_version instead of the BUNDLE, which the schema that refuses a rollup status is built from. Both directions were reproduced on the real CLI at bd1062a1 before any change: a 0.2 profile over a legacy-0.1 bundle refused status: done while warning NOTHING, and a 0.1 profile over a 0.2 bundle warned where status is only the lifecycle key. The detector now takes the scanned bundle states, evaluates each through profileForBundle, and dedupes by type so N 0.1 bundles still warn exactly once; tests now vary bundle state rather than only the profile version, three end-to-end cases replace a vacuous built-in test, and reverting the gate reddens exactly the five bundle-state tests and leaves the other nine green. Gates on the fixed head: bun test 5144 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail, typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, lore check exit 0 with 4 profiles read and 0 over capacity.
